label: first copy-phase step after <DEL> echoing original token i (L>=6)
explanation: Fires only at the step right after <DEL> (recall_idx 1, prev_tok <DEL>) when the fed-back input is the letter i, i.e. sequences whose first original token is i, and only for lengths L >= 6. Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, at any other copy step, or for L <= 5. Magnitude rises with L: L=6 contributes 4% of mass and is where most false positives sit (weak or zero activation), while L=9 carries 41%. Insensitive to which token is being output or to later tokens. The few misses are near-zero activations on other first tokens (mostly 2 or m).

issues: The test score reproduces: P 0.925, R 0.994, F1 0.958, mass recall 0.9997. The feature never fires in the original or delimiter phases, never at recall_idx other than 1, and never at L<=5 (the L==5 predicate has 0 actives). All activation comes right after a <DEL> prev_tok.

Every false positive is at L=6, and this is systematic. With the L==6 predicate, test precision is 0.694, while L=7, 8 and 9 each have precision 1.0. So about 31% of L=6 sequences that start with i stay silent. I found no history variable that cleanly separates them: n_digits, in_count, out_tok class and orig(5) being a digit move precision only between 0.54 and 0.85. It looks like a graded magnitude threshold in L, with L=6 near the cutoff. The explanation already says this.
A minor factual slip: the misses are mostly first token 2 (39 on dev), then o (7) and u (6). m has only 2, so 'mostly 2 or m' is inaccurate. The misses hold about 0% of the activation mass.
Tightening to L>=7 gives precision 1.0 but test F1 drops to 0.896, so the original predicate is the better tradeoff.
